page: Amazon Web Services c8gd.8xlarge is an arm64 compute-optimized server powered by AWS Graviton processors based on the ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 architecture. The instance provides 32 dedicated physical cores clocked at 2.8 GHz with a 1:1 thread-to-core mapping, eliminating hyper-threading resource contention. Memory capacity is allocated at 64.0 GB, yielding a 2.0 GB per core compute-focused ratio. In addition to Nitro hypervisor virtualization, the server bundles 1900 GB of local NVMe SSD instance storage and delivers a 15 Gbps baseline network bandwidth.

Benchmark results demonstrate exceptional multi-core throughput and memory subsystem performance. The instance achieves top-tier results in Geekbench multi-core workloads (21,489.0) and PassMark database operations (46,924.96). Memory bandwidth is a primary architectural highlight, reaching 384.64 GB/sec for large-block uncached reads and 170.56 GB/sec for writes, both ranking in the top 10% of evaluated systems. Workloads requiring sustained multi-threading, such as Clang software compilation and bzip3 decompression, perform in the top 25%.

Single-core execution metrics and large-scale language model inference expose clear hardware tradeoffs. Single-threaded performance across stress-ng and Geekbench falls in the median 50% band, reflecting the conservative 2.8 GHz clock speed. While small and medium LLM inference shows stable average throughput, large 70B model prompt processing falls into the lower 25% bracket due to the lack of dedicated GPU hardware acceleration and the strict 64 GB memory ceiling.

The 1:2 RAM-to-vCPU ratio and high memory bandwidth provide strong qualitative compute efficiency for CPU-bound applications that require low-latency scratch space. AWS c8gd.8xlarge is well aligned for multi-threaded distributed build pipelines, Redis caching clusters, high-throughput static web serving, and database workloads benefiting from local NVMe IOPS.
